## Scientific Question

Can macroscopic cosmological expansion laws emerge geometrically from discrete, parameter-free growth rules of higher-dimensional cut-and-project quasicrystals, bridging discrete Planck-scale tiling spaces with large-scale cosmic evolution?

## Mathematical Formulation & Derived Scaling Law

Building on foundational tiling-space cosmology models developed with **Aman Yadav** [@amaral2024tiling] and earlier continuum-bridge investigations of quasiperiodic metrics with Loop Quantum Gravity corrections [@amaral2017anamorphic], the companion computational investigation [`tiling-space-cosmology`](https://github.com/macielamaral/tiling-space-cosmology) (*Emergent Cosmology from Quasicrystal Growth: A Derived Scaling Law* [@amaral2025tiling_software]) models spatial configurations as growing cut-and-project quasicrystals generated by shell-by-shell projection of the 8-dimensional $E_8$ lattice into a 3D physical subspace. Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ index the discrete $E_8$ norm shell ($|x|^2 = 2n$). Defining an emergent cosmological scale factor $a(n)$ via typical inter-point spacing (measured robustly through quantile $k$-nearest-neighbor distances in 3D physical space), lattice shell combinatorics and outer-scale window geometry yield a parameter-free asymptotic scaling envelope:

$$
a(n) \asymp n^{5/6} \qquad (n \gg 1),
$$

superimposed with characteristic discrete staircase modulations induced by successive shell injections.

## Reproducible Simulation Code

The public MIT-licensed repository [`tiling-space-cosmology`](https://github.com/macielamaral/tiling-space-cosmology) provides Python 3.9+ scripts that generate shell-by-shell $E_8$ projections, compute quantile $k$-NN scale-factor estimators $a(n)$, and test the $n^{5/6}$ scaling law numerically.
